Consider the necessary care for this emergent situation.

Emergency management – [No technical training is given at this time]

Assess and protect airway Keep patient in a semi-reclined position if tolerated Immediately provide supplemental oxygen, if available Assess vital signs Consider administering nitroglycerine to the patient Reduce precipitating factors that may be contributing to the onset of pain If stabilized: use gauze to slow blood, suture wound closed & transfer to oral surgeon. With delayed recovery, call 911

Prevention – Angina is often triggered by stress or exertion. Consider length of appointment, pain control during treatment, and consider using psychosedation (based on medical assessment). Consider administering patient prescribed nitroglycerin prophylactically prior to start of procedure. Consider referring to oral surgeon initially.
